newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian military to get $40 million in U.S. aid.
newsitem.headline: Colombian military to get $40 million in U.S. aid.

text.p: Colombia's armed forces will receive $40.5 million in U.S. aid this month to help finance the country's drug war, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.

A ministry statement said the aid, in both equipment and training, would be disbursed within the next few days and three-quarters of it had been earmarked for the military, with the rest going to the National Police.
The equipment includes nine river patrol boats, five C-26 airplanes, 15 all-terrain vehicles and 32 UH-1H "Huey" helicopters.

The aid is part of the $112 million President Bill Clinton announced last week as additional U.S. support for anti-drug operations in Colombia, Mexico, Venezuela, Peru and eastern Caribbean countries.

A thin line separates support for anti-drug efforts and for counterinsurgency programmes in Colombia, since the government and military accuse guerrillas of increasing involvement in the country's lucrative drug trade.
